1→# Autonomous Claude Setup (Local Instructions)
     2→
     3→This file is not tracked by git. It contains setup instructions for running autonomous Claude Code locally.
     4→
     5→## Prerequisites
     6→
     7→- Claude Code CLI installed and authenticated (Max plan)
     8→- GitHub CLI (`gh`) authenticated
     9→- Node.js installed
    10→
    11→## Setup
    12→
    13→### 1. Install Continuous-Claude
    14→
    15→```bash
    16→# Install via curl (not npm)
    17→curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnandChowdhary/continuous-claude/main/install.sh | bash
    18→```
    19→
    20→**Requirements:**
    21→- Claude Code CLI (already have)
    22→- GitHub CLI (`gh`) - authenticated
    23→- `jq` - install with `brew install jq`
    24→
    25→### 2. Run Continuous-Claude
    26→
    27→```bash
    28→# Run continuously (polls for issues with 'claude' label)
    29→continuous-claude --owner bcamarneiro --repo adamastor
    30→
    31→# Or run once (for testing)
    32→continuous-claude --owner bcamarneiro --repo adamastor --once
    33→```
    34→
    35→### 3. (Optional) Auto-start with launchd
    36→
    37→Create `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.adamastor.continuous-claude.plist`:
    38→
    39→```xml
    40→<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
    41→<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
    42→<plist version="1.0">
    43→<dict>
    44→    <key>Label</key>
    45→    <string>com.adamastor.continuous-claude</string>
    46→    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    47→    <array>
    48→        <string>/usr/local/bin/continuous-claude</string>
    49→        <string>--owner</string>
    50→        <string>bcamarneiro</string>
    51→        <string>--repo</string>
    52→        <string>adamastor</string>
    53→    </array>
    54→    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    55→    <true/>
    56→    <key>KeepAlive</key>
    57→    <true/>
    58→    <key>StandardOutPath</key>
    59→    <string>/tmp/continuous-claude.log</string>
    60→    <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
    61→    <string>/tmp/continuous-claude.error.log</string>
    62→</dict>
    63→</plist>
    64→```
    65→
    66→Load: `launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.adamastor.continuous-claude.plist`
    67→Unload: `launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.adamastor.continuous-claude.plist`
    68→Check logs: `tail -f /tmp/continuous-claude.log`
    69→
    70→## Workflow
    71→
    72→1. Create/triage issues on GitHub
    73→2. Add `claude` label to issues you want AI to handle
    74→3. Continuous-Claude picks it up (runs locally, uses Max plan)
    75→4. Claude creates branch, implements fix, opens PR
    76→5. You review and merge
    77→
    78→## Labels
    79→
    80→| Label | Meaning |
    81→|-------|---------|
    82→| `claude` | AI should work on this issue |
    83→| `needs-clarification` | AI needs more info |
    84→| `ai-blocked` | AI couldn't complete |
    85→
    86→## Cost
    87→
    88→**Free** - uses your existing Max plan CLI authentication.

    20→- **Use workspace commands** - `bun --filter watcher test`, `bun --filter web build`
    21→
    22→### Change Scope
    23→
    24→- **Small, focused changes** - One feature, one bug fix, one refactor per PR
    25→- **Clear commit messages** - Describe what changed and why
    26→- **Incremental improvements** - Build up complex features in small steps
    27→
    28→### Branching Strategy
    29→
    30→- **All PRs target `staging`** - Never create PRs directly to `main`
    31→- **Create feature branches from `staging`** - `git checkout staging && git pull && git checkout -b <type>/issue-<n>-<desc>`
    32→- **Branch naming**: `fix/`, `feat/`, `refactor/`, `docs/`, `chore/` + issue number + short description
    33→

    35→
    36→## Tool-Specific Guidance
    37→
    38→### Inline Assistants (GitHub Copilot, Cursor Inline)
    39→
    40→**Best for:**
    41→- Single function changes
    42→- Component prop additions
    43→- Type definitions
    44→- Small utility functions
    45→

    50→

    62→- ✅ "Update ARCHITECTURE.md to document the new attendance scraping incremental logic"
    63→- ❌ "Make the UI better" (too vague, no scope)
    64→
    65→### PR Reviewers (GitHub Copilot Reviews)
    66→
    67→**Best for:**
    68→- Code review feedback
    69→- Identifying potential bugs
    70→- Suggesting improvements
    71→
    72→**To help AI reviewers:**
    73→- Write clear PR descriptions (see [PR Template](../.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md))
    74→- Include "What", "Why", "How", and "Testing" sections
    75→- Link related issues
    76→- Highlight risks and breaking changes
    77→
    78→### Responding to PR Review Comments
    79→
    80→When reviewing PRs or addressing Copilot comments, **always leave a reply** on each comment:
    81→
    82→1. **Reply format for addressed comments**:
    83→
    84→   ```text

    98→## Critical Paths (Handle with Extra Care)
    99→

   101→
   102→### 1. Transform Pipeline (`apps/watcher/src/transform/`)
   103→
   104→**Why critical:** This is the core data processing logic. Errors here affect data accuracy.
   105→
   106→**Guidelines:**
   107→- Test each transform step independently
   108→- Understand step dependencies (see [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md#the-transform-pipeline))
   109→- Maintain ID mappings correctly (DepId, DepCadId, biography_id)
   110→- Add tests when modifying transform logic
   111→
   112→**Example safe change:**
   113→```typescript
   114→// Adding a new field to party transform

   116→  return parties.map(p => ({

   134→

   136→
   137→**Locations:**

   148→**Current formula:**

     2→
     3→This file provides instructions for Auto-Claude agents working on Adamastor issues.
     4→
     5→## Critical Rules
     6→
     7→1. **Branch from staging** - All branches MUST be created from `staging`, never from `main`
     8→2. **PRs target staging** - All pull requests MUST target `staging`, never `main`
     9→3. **Regression tests required** - Every bug fix MUST include an E2E regression test
    10→4. **Reply to all PR comments** - Never leave review comments without responses
    11→5. **Wait for CI** - Do not request review until all CI checks are green
    12→
    13→## Complete Workflow
    14→
    15→### 1. Branch Creation
    16→```bash

    18→git pull origin staging

    21→- Types: `fix/`, `feat/`, `refactor/`, `docs/`, `chore/`

    23→

    29→

    31→- Read relevant files
    32→- Reproduce the problem (for bugs)
    33→- Implement the fix or feature
    34→- Run tests: `bun run test`
    35→

    39→- `navigation.spec.ts` - Navigation bugs

    49→  // Test the specific user flow that was broken
    50→});

    52→
    53→Test locally: `cd apps/web && npx playwright test <spec-file>`
    54→
    55→### 5. Commit
    56→Format: `<type>(<scope>): <description> (#<issue-number>)`

    59→
    60→### 6. Create PR

1→# Auto-Claude Configuration for Adamastor

     3→This file provides instructions for Auto-Claude agents working on Adamastor issues.
     4→
     5→## Critical Rules
     6→
     7→1. **Branch from staging** - All branches MUST be created from `staging`, never from `main`
     8→2. **PRs target staging** - All pull requests MUST target `staging`, never `main`
     9→3. **Regression tests required** - Every bug fix MUST include an E2E regression test
    10→4. **Reply to all PR comments** - Never leave review comments without responses
    11→5. **Wait for CI** - Do not request review until all CI checks are green
    12→
    13→## Complete Workflow
    14→
    15→### 1. Branch Creation
    16→```bash
    17→git checkout staging
    18→git pull origin staging
    19→git checkout -b <type>/issue-<number>-<short-description>
    20→```
    21→- Types: `fix/`, `feat/`, `refactor/`, `docs/`, `chore/`
    22→- Example: `fix/issue-42-district-filter`
    23→
    24→### 2. Issue Comment
    25→Post a comment on the issue stating:
    26→- What you're working on
    27→- Your planned approach
    28→- Any questions or clarifications
    29→
    30→### 3. Implementation
    31→- Read relevant files
    32→- Reproduce the problem (for bugs)
    33→- Implement the fix or feature
    34→- Run tests: `bun run test`
    35→
    36→### 4. E2E Regression Test (Bug Fixes Only)
    37→**MANDATORY** for all bug fixes. Add test to appropriate spec file in `apps/web/e2e/`:
    38→- `home.spec.ts` - Homepage bugs
    39→- `navigation.spec.ts` - Navigation bugs
    40→- `leaderboard.spec.ts` - Ranking page bugs
    41→- `postal-codes.spec.ts` - Postal code bugs
    42→- `parties.spec.ts` - Party page bugs
    43→
    44→Pattern:
    45→```typescript
    46→// Issue #XX: Brief title
    47→// @see https://github.com/bcamarneiro/adamastor/issues/XX
    48→test('descriptive test name', async ({ page }) => {
    49→  // Test the specific user flow that was broken
    50→});
    51→```
    52→
    53→Test locally: `cd apps/web && npx playwright test <spec-file>`
    54→
    55→### 5. Commit
    56→Format: `<type>(<scope>): <description> (#<issue-number>)`
    57→- Example: `fix(web): resolve district filter 400 error (#42)`
    58→- Types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`
    59→
    60→### 6. Create PR
    61→```bash
    62→git push -u origin <branch-name>
    63→gh pr create --base staging --title "..." --body "Closes #<number>
    64→
    65→## What
    66→[Brief description]
    67→
    68→## Why
    69→[Why this change is needed]
    70→
    71→## How

    78→"
    79→```
    80→
    81→**CRITICAL**: Use `--base staging`, NOT `--base main`.
    82→
    83→### 7. Wait for CI and Check for Copilot Comments
    84→
    85→#### Step 7a: Wait for CI to complete
    86→
    87→```bash
    88→gh run watch <run-id>
    89→```
    90→
    91→- All checks must pass: lint, typecheck, test-watcher, test-web, e2e, build
    92→- If CI fails, fix and push again
    93→
    94→#### Step 7b: Check for GitHub Copilot review comments
    95→
    96→**CRITICAL**: Before marking as ready for human review, check if Copilot already left comments:
    97→
    98→```bash

   100→gh pr view <number> --json reviews,comments --jq '.reviews[], .comments[]'
   101→```
   102→
   103→If Copilot (or any automated reviewer) left comments:
   104→
   105→1. Address ALL comments following step 8 below

   107→3. Wait for CI to pass again

   111→**Never send a PR to human review with:**

   116→
   117→### 8. Address PR Review Comments
   118→If the PR receives review comments (from Copilot or humans):

# Auto-Claude Configuration for Adamastor

This file provides instructions for Auto-Claude agents working on Adamastor issues.

## Critical Rules

1. **Branch from staging** - All branches MUST be created from `staging`, never from `main`
2. **PRs target staging** - All pull requests MUST target `staging`, never `main`
3. **Regression tests required** - Every bug fix MUST include an E2E regression test
4. **Reply to all PR comments** - Never leave review comments without responses
5. **Wait for CI** - Do not request review until all CI checks are green

## Complete Workflow

### 1. Branch Creation
```bash
git checkout staging
git pull origin staging
git checkout -b <type>/issue-<number>-<short-description>
```
- Types: `fix/`, `feat/`, `refactor/`, `docs/`, `chore/`
- Example: `fix/issue-42-district-filter`

### 2. Issue Comment
Post a comment on the issue stating:
- What you're working on
- Your planned approach
- Any questions or clarifications

### 3. Implementation
- Read relevant files
- Reproduce the problem (for bugs)
- Implement the fix or feature
- Run tests: `bun run test`

### 4. E2E Regression Test (Bug Fixes Only)
**MANDATORY** for all bug fixes. Add test to appropriate spec file in `apps/web/e2e/`:
- `home.spec.ts` - Homepage bugs
- `navigation.spec.ts` - Navigation bugs
- `leaderboard.spec.ts` - Ranking page bugs
- `postal-codes.spec.ts` - Postal code bugs
- `parties.spec.ts` - Party page bugs

Pattern:
```typescript
// Issue #XX: Brief title
// @see https://github.com/bcamarneiro/adamastor/issues/XX
test('descriptive test name', async ({ page }) => {
  // Test the specific user flow that was broken
});
```

Test locally: `cd apps/web && npx playwright test <spec-file>`

### 5. Commit
Format: `<type>(<scope>): <description> (#<issue-number>)`
- Example: `fix(web): resolve district filter 400 error (#42)`
- Types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`

### 6. Create PR
```bash
git push -u origin <branch-name>
gh pr create --base staging --title "..." --body "Closes #<number>

## What
[Brief description]

## Why
[Why this change is needed]

## How
[Implementation details]

## Testing
- [ ] Unit tests pass
- [ ] E2E tests pass (for bug fixes)
- [ ] Manual testing completed
"
```

**CRITICAL**: Use `--base staging`, NOT `--base main`.

### 7. Wait for CI and Check for Copilot Comments

#### Step 7a: Wait for CI to complete

```bash
gh run watch <run-id>
```

- All checks must pass: lint, typecheck, test-watcher, test-web, e2e, build
- If CI fails, fix and push again

#### Step 7b: Check for GitHub Copilot review comments

**CRITICAL**: Before marking as ready for human review, check if Copilot already left comments:

```bash
# Check for any review comments
gh pr view <number> --json reviews,comments --jq '.reviews[], .comments[]'
```

If Copilot (or any automated reviewer) left comments:

1. Address ALL comments following step 8 below
2. Push fixes
3. Wait for CI to pass again
4. Verify all comments have replies
5. Only then mark as ready for human review

**Never send a PR to human review with:**

- ❌ Failing CI checks
- ❌ Unaddressed Copilot comments
- ❌ Review comments without replies

### 8. Address PR Review Comments
If the PR receives review comments (from Copilot or humans):

1. Check for comments:
   ```bash
   gh pr view <number> --comments
   ```

2. For each comment:
   - Make the fix if appropriate
   - Reply individually:
     ```bash
     gh api repos/bcamarneiro/adamastor/pulls/comments/<comment-id>/replies \
       -f body="Fixed in commit <sha>. <description>"
     ```
   - OR explain why not changing:
     ```bash
     gh api repos/bcamarneiro/adamastor/pulls/comments/<comment-id>/replies \
       -f body="Won't fix: <reasoning>"
     ```

3. After addressing all comments:
   - Push fixes
   - Wait for CI to pass
   - Re-request review:
     ```bash
     gh pr edit <number> --add-reviewer @bcamarneiro
     ```

**CRITICAL**: Every comment must receive a reply.

## Project Context

**What is Adamastor?**
Portuguese Parliament transparency platform tracking deputy attendance and performance.

**Tech Stack:**
- Monorepo with Turborepo
- Bun (watcher), Vite (web)
- TypeScript (strict mode)
- Testing: Bun test (watcher), Vitest + Playwright E2E (web)
- Database: Supabase (PostgreSQL)
- UI: React + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS
- Linting: Biome (not ESLint/Prettier)

**Key Files:**
- `apps/watcher/src/transform/` - Data pipeline (CRITICAL: affects data accuracy)
- `apps/web/e2e/*.spec.ts` - E2E regression tests
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` - Shared TypeScript types
- `supabase/migrations/*.sql` - Database migrations

**Portuguese Context:**
- **Legislatura** - Legislative term (currently XVII/17th)
- **Deputado** - Deputy/MP
- **Distrito** - Electoral district (22 total)
- **Partido** - Political party (PS, PSD, CH, IL, BE, etc.)

## Common Pitfalls to Avoid

❌ Branching from `main` instead of `staging`
❌ Creating PRs to `main` instead of `staging`
❌ Forgetting E2E regression tests for bug fixes
❌ Leaving PR review comments without replies
❌ Requesting review before CI passes
❌ Using `any` types in TypeScript
❌ Modifying existing database migrations (create new ones)
❌ Committing secrets or API keys

## Testing Commands

```bash
# Root level
bun install          # Install all dependencies
bun lint             # Lint all packages (Biome)
bun typecheck        # Type check all packages

# App-specific
bun --filter watcher test    # Run watcher unit tests
bun --filter web test        # Run web unit tests
bun --filter web build       # Build web app

# E2E tests
cd apps/web && npx playwright test
cd apps/web && npx playwright test home.spec.ts  # Run specific spec
```

- Full AI guidelines: `docs/AI_AGENTS.md`
- GitHub Copilot context: `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- Architecture: `ARCHITECTURE.md`
- Contributing: `CONTRIBUTING.md`

=============================================

- Models and enums: workspace/models.py
- Git utilities: workspace/git_utils.py
- Setup functions: workspace/setup.py

- Finalization: workspace/finalization.py
- Complex merge operations: remain here (workspace.py)

Public API is exported via workspace/__init__.py for backward compatibility.

"""
Tool Models and Constants
==========================

Defines tool name constants and configuration for auto-claude MCP tools.

This module is the single source of truth for all tool definitions used by
the Claude Agent SDK client. Tool lists are organized by category:

- Base tools: Core file operations (Read, Write, Edit, etc.)
- Web tools: Documentation and research (WebFetch, WebSearch)
- MCP tools: External integrations (Context7, Linear, Graphiti, etc.)
- Auto-Claude tools: Custom build management tools
"""

import os

# =============================================================================
# Base Tools (Built-in Claude Code tools)
# =============================================================================

# Core file operation tools
BASE_READ_TOOLS = ["Read", "Glob", "Grep"]
BASE_WRITE_TOOLS = ["Write", "Edit", "Bash"]

# Web tools for documentation lookup and research
# Always available to all agents for accessing external information
WEB_TOOLS = ["WebFetch", "WebSearch"]

# =============================================================================
# Auto-Claude MCP Tools (Custom build management)
# =============================================================================

# Auto-Claude MCP tool names (prefixed with mcp__auto-claude__)
TOOL_UPDATE_SUBTASK_STATUS = "mcp__auto-claude__update_subtask_status"
TOOL_GET_BUILD_PROGRESS = "mcp__auto-claude__get_build_progress"
TOOL_RECORD_DISCOVERY = "mcp__auto-claude__record_discovery"
TOOL_RECORD_GOTCHA = "mcp__auto-claude__record_gotcha"
TOOL_GET_SESSION_CONTEXT = "mcp__auto-claude__get_session_context"
TOOL_UPDATE_QA_STATUS = "mcp__auto-claude__update_qa_status"

# =============================================================================
# External MCP Tools
# =============================================================================

# Context7 MCP tools for documentation lookup (always enabled)
CONTEXT7_TOOLS = [
    "mcp__context7__resolve-library-id",
    "mcp__context7__get-library-docs",
]

# Linear MCP tools for project management (when LINEAR_API_KEY is set)
LINEAR_TOOLS = [
    "mcp__linear-server__list_teams",
    "mcp__linear-server__get_team",
    "mcp__linear-server__list_projects",
    "mcp__linear-server__get_project",
    "mcp__linear-server__create_project",
    "mcp__linear-server__update_project",
    "mcp__linear-server__list_issues",
    "mcp__linear-server__get_issue",
    "mcp__linear-server__create_issue",
    "mcp__linear-server__update_issue",
    "mcp__linear-server__list_comments",
    "mcp__linear-server__create_comment",
    "mcp__linear-server__list_issue_statuses",
    "mcp__linear-server__list_issue_labels",
    "mcp__linear-server__list_users",
    "mcp__linear-server__get_user",
]

# Graphiti MCP tools for knowledge graph memory (when GRAPHITI_MCP_URL is set)
# See: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti
GRAPHITI_MCP_TOOLS = [
    "mcp__graphiti-memory__search_nodes",  # Search entity summaries
    "mcp__graphiti-memory__search_facts",  # Search relationships between entities
    "mcp__graphiti-memory__add_episode",  # Add data to knowledge graph
    "mcp__graphiti-memory__get_episodes",  # Retrieve recent episodes
    "mcp__graphiti-memory__get_entity_edge",  # Get specific entity/relationship
]

# =============================================================================
# Browser Automation MCP Tools (QA agents only)
# =============================================================================

# Puppeteer MCP tools for web browser automation
# Used for web frontend validation (non-Electron web apps)
# NOTE: Screenshots must be compressed (1280x720, quality 60, JPEG) to stay under
# Claude SDK's 1MB JSON message buffer limit. See GitHub issue #74.
PUPPETEER_TOOLS = [
    "mcp__puppeteer__puppeteer_connect_active_tab",
    "mcp__puppeteer__puppeteer_navigate",
    "mcp__puppeteer__puppeteer_screenshot",
    "mcp__puppeteer__puppeteer_click",
    "mcp__puppeteer__puppeteer_fill",
    "mcp__puppeteer__puppeteer_select",
    "mcp__puppeteer__puppeteer_hover",
    "mcp__puppeteer__puppeteer_evaluate",
]

# Uses electron-mcp-server to connect to Electron apps via Chrome DevTools Protocol.
# Electron app must be started with --remote-debugging-port=9222 (or ELECTRON_DEBUG_PORT).
# These tools are only available to QA agents (qa_reviewer, qa_fixer), not Coder/Planner.
# NOTE: Screenshots must be compressed to stay under Claude SDK's 1MB JSON message buffer limit.
ELECTRON_TOOLS = [
    "mcp__electron__get_electron_window_info",  # Get info about running Electron windows
    "mcp__electron__take_screenshot",  # Capture screenshot of Electron window
    "mcp__electron__send_command_to_electron",  # Send commands (click, fill, evaluate JS)
    "mcp__electron__read_electron_logs",  # Read console logs from Electron app
]

# =============================================================================
# Configuration
# =============================================================================


def is_electron_mcp_enabled() -> bool:
    """
    Check if Electron MCP server integration is enabled.

    Requires ELECTRON_MCP_ENABLED to be set to 'true'.
    When enabled, QA agents can use Electron MCP tools to connect to Electron apps
    via Chrome DevTools Protocol on the configured debug port.
    """
    return os.environ.get("ELECTRON_MCP_ENABLED", "").lower() == "true"

    },
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # BUILD PHASES (Full tools + Graphiti memory)
    # Note: "linear" is conditional on project setting "update_linear_with_tasks"

    "planner": {

"""
QA Management Tools
===================

Tools for managing QA status and sign-off in implementation_plan.json.
"""

import json
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

try:
    from claude_agent_sdk import tool

    SDK_TOOLS_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    SDK_TOOLS_AVAILABLE = False
    tool = None


def _push_branch_to_remote(
    worktree_path: Path,
    branch_name: str,
) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """
    Push a branch to the remote origin.

    Handles:
    - First-time push with -u flag to set upstream
    - Existing remote branch with --force-with-lease for safety

    Args:
        worktree_path: Path to worktree to push from
        branch_name: Name of the branch to push

    Returns:
        Tuple of (success: bool, message: str)
    """
    # First try a normal push with -u to set upstream
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "push", "-u", "origin", branch_name],
        cwd=worktree_path,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        errors="replace",
    )

    if result.returncode == 0:
        return True, f"Branch '{branch_name}' pushed successfully"

    # Check if it's a rejected push (remote has changes)
    if "rejected" in result.stderr or "non-fast-forward" in result.stderr:
        # Try with --force-with-lease for safety
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "push", "--force-with-lease", "-u", "origin", branch_name],
            cwd=worktree_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            encoding="utf-8",
            errors="replace",
        )

        if result.returncode == 0:
            return True, f"Branch '{branch_name}' pushed successfully (force-with-lease)"

    # Check for authentication issues
    if "Authentication" in result.stderr or "permission" in result.stderr.lower():
        return False, f"Authentication error: Please ensure 'gh auth login' or git credentials are configured. Details: {result.stderr.strip()}"

    # Check for network issues
    if "Could not resolve" in result.stderr or "unable to access" in result.stderr.lower():
        return False, f"Network error: Could not connect to remote. Details: {result.stderr.strip()}"

    # Generic failure
    error_msg = result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip() or "Unknown error"
    return False, f"Push failed: {error_msg}"


def _get_worktree_branch(worktree_path: Path) -> str | None:
    """Get the current branch name from a worktree."""
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"],
        cwd=worktree_path,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        errors="replace",
    )
    if result.returncode == 0:
        return result.stdout.strip()
    return None


def _get_worktree_path_from_spec(spec_dir: Path) -> Path | None:
    """
    Get the worktree path for a spec directory.

    Spec directories are typically at:
    - .auto-claude/specs/{spec-name}/

    Worktrees are at:
    - .worktrees/{spec-name}/
    """
    spec_name = spec_dir.name

    # Navigate up to find the project root
    # spec_dir is like: /path/to/project/.auto-claude/specs/{spec-name}
    # or in worktree: /path/to/project/.worktrees/{spec-name}/.auto-claude/specs/{spec-name}

    # Check if we're in a worktree (spec_dir contains .worktrees in path)
    spec_path_str = str(spec_dir)
    if ".worktrees/" in spec_path_str:
        # Extract the worktree path
        # e.g., /path/.worktrees/spec-name/.auto-claude/specs/spec-name
        # worktree is at /path/.worktrees/spec-name
        worktrees_idx = spec_path_str.find(".worktrees/")
        if worktrees_idx != -1:
            # Find the next / after .worktrees/
            after_worktrees = spec_path_str[worktrees_idx + len(".worktrees/"):]
            next_slash = after_worktrees.find("/")
            if next_slash != -1:
                worktree_name = after_worktrees[:next_slash]
                project_root = Path(spec_path_str[:worktrees_idx])
                worktree_path = project_root / ".worktrees" / worktree_name
                if worktree_path.exists():
                    return worktree_path

    # Check in standard location relative to spec parent dirs
    # spec_dir is: project/.auto-claude/specs/{spec-name}
    # worktree is: project/.worktrees/{spec-name}
    project_root = spec_dir.parent.parent.parent  # Up from specs/{spec-name} to project root
    worktree_path = project_root / ".worktrees" / spec_name
    if worktree_path.exists():
        return worktree_path

    return None


def create_qa_tools(spec_dir: Path, project_dir: Path) -> list:
    """
    Create QA management tools.

    Args:
        spec_dir: Path to the spec directory
        project_dir: Path to the project root

    Returns:
        List of QA tool functions
    """
    if not SDK_TOOLS_AVAILABLE:
        return []

    tools = []

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tool: update_qa_status
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    @tool(
        "update_qa_status",
        "Update the QA sign-off status in implementation_plan.json. Use after QA review.",
        {"status": str, "issues": str, "tests_passed": str},
    )
    async def update_qa_status(args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Update QA status in the implementation plan."""
        status = args["status"]
        issues_str = args.get("issues", "[]")
        tests_str = args.get("tests_passed", "{}")

        valid_statuses = [
            "pending",
            "in_review",
            "approved",
            "rejected",
            "fixes_applied",
        ]
        if status not in valid_statuses:
            return {
                "content": [
                    {
                        "type": "text",
                        "text": f"Error: Invalid QA status '{status}'. Must be one of: {valid_statuses}",
                    }
                ]
            }

        plan_file = spec_dir / "implementation_plan.json"
        if not plan_file.exists():
            return {
                "content": [
                    {
                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "Error: implementation_plan.json not found",
                    }
                ]
            }

        try:
            # Parse issues and tests
            try:
                issues = json.loads(issues_str) if issues_str else []
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                issues = [{"description": issues_str}] if issues_str else []

            try:
                tests_passed = json.loads(tests_str) if tests_str else {}
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                tests_passed = {}

            with open(plan_file) as f:
                plan = json.load(f)

            # Get current QA session number
            current_qa = plan.get("qa_signoff", {})
            qa_session = current_qa.get("qa_session", 0)
            if status in ["in_review", "rejected"]:
                qa_session += 1

            plan["qa_signoff"] = {
                "status": status,
                "qa_session": qa_session,
                "issues_found": issues,
                "tests_passed": tests_passed,
                "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                "ready_for_qa_revalidation": status == "fixes_applied",

            push_message = ""

            # This ensures the UI shows the correct column after QA

                # When QA approves, push the branch to remote before transitioning to human_review
                worktree_path = _get_worktree_path_from_spec(spec_dir)

                if worktree_path:
                    branch_name = _get_worktree_branch(worktree_path)

                    if branch_name:
                        # Set status to pushing_branch during push
                        plan["status"] = "pushing_branch"
                        plan["planStatus"] = "pushing"

                        # Record branch_pushed status

1→# Specification: Auto-Claude PR Creation Before Human Review
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→Currently, when using auto-claude, the workflow completes by staging changes to the main project and marking the task as "human_review" - requiring the user to manually commit and create a PR. The user wants the workflow to automatically create a Pull Request after QA approval, so that human review happens in GitHub where CI status is visible. This eliminates manual terminal operations and enables validation through GitHub's PR interface.
     6→
     7→## Workflow Type

    23→- [ ] Store PR URL in `implementation_plan.json`

    94→
    95→### PR Creation Pattern
    96→
    97→From `AUTO_CLAUDE.md`:
    98→
    99→```bash
   100→git push -u origin <branch-name>
   101→gh pr create --base staging --title "..." --body "Closes #<number>
   102→

   105→

   136→  "stagedInMainProject": true

   141→```json
   142→{
   143→  "pr_created": {
   144→    "url": "https://github.com/bcamarneiro/adamastor/pull/123",
   145→    "number": 123,

   147→    "created_at": "2026-01-07T22:28:00.000Z"
   148→  },
   149→  "status": "human_review"
   150→}
   151→```
   152→
   153→## Requirements
   154→
   155→### Functional Requirements
   156→
   157→1. **Automatic PR Creation After QA Approval**
   158→   - Description: When QA agent approves a task, the workflow should automatically create a GitHub PR
   159→   - Acceptance: PR appears in GitHub repository after QA approval, before status changes to "human_review"
   160→
   161→2. **Branch Push Before PR**
   162→   - Description: Worktree branch must be pushed to remote before PR creation
   163→   - Acceptance: `git push -u origin <branch>` succeeds without manual intervention
   164→
   165→3. **PR URL Tracking**
   166→   - Description: The PR URL must be recorded in `implementation_plan.json`
   167→   - Acceptance: `pr_created.url` field contains valid GitHub PR URL
   168→
   169→4. **Human Review Triggered by PR**
   170→   - Description: Status changes to "human_review" only after PR is successfully created
   171→   - Acceptance: `status: "human_review"` only appears in implementation_plan.json when `pr_created.url` is set
   172→
   173→5. **CI Status Visibility**
   174→   - Description: User can validate changes in GitHub UI where CI status is displayed
   175→   - Acceptance: PR page shows CI checks running/passed/failed
   176→
   177→### Edge Cases
   178→
   179→1. **Branch Push Failure** - Retry push, or mark task as "push_failed" with error message for manual intervention
   180→2. **PR Creation Failure** - Retry with exponential backoff, or mark task as "pr_creation_failed" with error details
   181→3. **Duplicate PR Exists** - Check for existing PR on branch before creating new one; link to existing if found
   182→4. **No GitHub CLI Auth** - Fail gracefully with clear error message about `gh auth login` requirement
   183→5. **Remote Branch Already Exists** - Use `git push --force-with-lease` for safety
   184→
   185→## Implementation Notes
   186→
   187→### DO
   188→- Follow the PR body format in `AUTO_CLAUDE.md` exactly
   189→- Use `gh pr create` with `--base staging` always
   190→- Store PR URL immediately after creation for tracking
   191→- Check for existing PRs before creating duplicates
   192→- Use meaningful PR titles derived from spec/task name
   193→
   194→### DON'T
   195→- Create PRs targeting `main` branch
   196→- Skip the branch push step (PR creation will fail)
   197→- Leave tasks in "human_review" without a PR URL
   198→- Use `git push --force` (prefer `--force-with-lease`)
   199→- Create PRs without running QA approval first

     4→
     5→Currently, when using auto-claude, the workflow completes by staging changes to the main project and marking the task as "human_review" - requiring the user to manually commit and create a PR. The user wants the workflow to automatically create a Pull Request after QA approval, so that human review happens in GitHub where CI status is visible. This eliminates manual terminal operations and enables validation through GitHub's PR interface.

   - **Retryable errors:** `network`, `timeout`, `rate_limit`, `server_error`, `unknown`
   - **Non-retryable errors:** `auth`, `exists`, `base_branch`, `not_found`, `gh_not_found`

       "message": str,         # Error message
       "error_type": str,      # Categorized error type
       "can_retry": bool,      # True if retryable
       "retry_count": int,     # Number of retries (0 initially)

4. **New `retry_pr_creation` MCP tool:**

   188→def _update_status_file_pr_url(spec_dir: Path, pr_url: str) -> bool:
   189→    """
   190→    Update the .auto-claude-status file with the PR URL.
   191→
   192→    This updates the status file in the MAIN project (not worktree).
   193→    The status file is used by ccstatusline for visibility.
   194→
   195→    Args:
   196→        spec_dir: Path to the spec directory
   197→        pr_url: GitHub PR URL to set
   198→
   199→    Returns:
   200→        True if successfully updated, False otherwise
   201→    """
   202→    try:
   203→        # Find the main project root (not the worktree)
   204→        # spec_dir patterns:
   205→        # - Main project: /project/.auto-claude/specs/{spec-name}
   206→        # - Worktree: /project/.worktrees/{spec-name}/.auto-claude/specs/{spec-name}
   207→        spec_path_str = str(spec_dir)
   208→
   209→        if ".worktrees/" in spec_path_str:
   210→            # In worktree - find main project root
   211→            worktrees_idx = spec_path_str.find(".worktrees/")
   212→            project_root = Path(spec_path_str[:worktrees_idx])
   213→        else:
   214→            # In main project - go up from specs/{spec-name}
   215→            project_root = spec_dir.parent.parent.parent
   216→
   217→        status_file = project_root / ".auto-claude-status"
   218→        if not status_file.exists():
   219→            # No status file yet - nothing to update
   220→            return False
   221→
   222→        # Read existing status
   223→        with open(status_file) as f:
   224→            status_data = json.load(f)
   225→
   226→        # Update the PR URL
   227→        status_data["pr_url"] = pr_url
   228→        status_data["last_update"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
   229→
   230→        # Write back
   231→        with open(status_file, "w") as f:
   232→            json.dump(status_data, f, indent=2)
   233→
   234→        return True
   235→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
   236→        # Non-fatal error - status file update is best-effort
   237→        return False
   238→
   239→
   240→def _generate_pr_title(plan: dict, spec_dir: Path) -> str:
   241→    """
   242→    Generate a PR title from the implementation plan.
   243→
   244→    Format: "<feature name>" or "auto-claude: <spec-name>" if no feature
   245→
   246→    Args:
   247→        plan: Implementation plan dictionary
   248→        spec_dir: Path to the spec directory
   249→
   250→    Returns:
   251→        PR title string
   252→    """
   253→    feature = plan.get("feature", "")
   254→    if feature:
   255→        return feature
   256→
   257→    # Fallback to spec directory name
   258→    spec_name = spec_dir.name
   259→    if spec_name:
   260→        # Remove leading number prefix if present (e.g., "022-" becomes "")
   261→        if "-" in spec_name:
   262→            parts = spec_name.split("-", 1)
   263→            if parts[0].isdigit() and len(parts) > 1:
   264→                # Make the slug more readable
   265→                slug = parts[1].replace("-", " ").title()
   266→                return f"auto-claude: {slug}"
   267→        return f"auto-claude: {spec_name}"
   268→
   269→    return "auto-claude: Implementation complete"
   270→
   271→
   272→def _generate_pr_body(plan: dict, spec_dir: Path) -> str:
   273→    """
   274→    Generate a PR body from the implementation plan.
   275→
   276→    Follows the AUTO_CLAUDE.md format:
   277→    - Closes #<issue> (if issue number detected)
   278→    - ## What: Brief description
   279→    - ## Why: Why this change is needed
   280→    - ## How: Implementation details
   281→    - ## Testing: Checklist

   299→        if parts[0].isdigit():
   300→            issue_number = int(parts[0])
   301→
   302→    # Add "Closes #<issue>" if we have an issue number
   303→    if issue_number:
   304→        lines.append(f"Closes #{issue_number}")
   305→        lines.append("")
   306→
   307→    # ## What section - use feature name and description
   308→    lines.append("## What")
   309→    feature = plan.get("feature", "")
   310→    description = plan.get("description", "")
   311→
   312→    if feature and description:
